catalog_quote: This is a preliminary study of the tone system of the Laze language as spoken in the township of Xiangjiao, Muli county, Sichuan ... Its tonal system is here described as being structured in terms of H(igh), M(id) and L(ow) levels, like that of the closely related languages Naxi and Na. There exist four lexical tones for Laze monosyllables; in theory, this could yield as many as sixteen tone patterns over disyllables, but only six are observed. ... The notion of 'phonological word' is used rather loosely to refer to the domain of tone, covering such syntactically different entities as a disyllabic lexical word, a compound noun, or a predicate made up of an object noun plus a verb. ... tonal change is the only phonological change which takes place when a disyllabic or polysyllabic entity ('phonological word') is created out of several distinct morphemes. ... In Laze, the situation is not…

tone_statements.citation: Michaud, Alexis, He Limin & Zhong Yaoping. 2017. Nàxī 納西 language / Naish languages. In Rint Sybesma et al. (eds.), Encyclopedia of Chinese Language and Linguistics, vol. 3, 144-157. Leiden: Brill. DOI 10.1163/2210-7363_ecll_COM_00000247. Open author version: HAL halshs-00793649v2 (CC BY-NC-SA).
tone_statements.quote: Tones in Naish languages consist simply of pitch distinctions, on a three-level scale: High, Mid and Low, without phonation-type characteristics. Contours are made up of sequences of tone levels realized on a single syllable. ... e.g. /35/ for a Mid-to-High rise (as in Laze /ʈʰæ35/ ‘to bite’). ... In Yongning Na and Laze, there is overwhelming evidence from alternations showing that contours consist of sequences of levels ... All syllables have tone in the surface phonological representation in Na and Laze, although some bound morphemes do not have a tone of their own.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.1.4 Tones, i. inventory and ii. Distribution; author version halshs-00793649v2 (published pp. 144-157, no page numbers in this version)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones H M L; rising contours (LM, MH) on monosyllables are level sequences per reassociation alternations; no falling contours; C(G)V+T. Floating H given for Na only. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Michaud, Alexis. 2013. Studying level-tone systems in Asia: the case of the Naish languages. Proc. International Conference on Phonetics of the Languages in China (ICPLC-2013), Hong Kong, 1-6. HAL halshs-00868019.
sources.quote: Laze characterised as a canonical level-tone system; the only 'de-stressing' remark (PDF p.3) concerns Naxi reduplications, not Laze.
sources.locator: Abstract, p.2: 'the tones of Laze and Yongning Na fall squarely in the level-tone type, whereas Naxi is somewhat of an outlier among level-tone systems.'
sources.note: Later typological statement by the same author placing Laze 'squarely in the level-tone type'. downloaded: confirms.

sources.citation: Michaud, Alexis & Guillaume Jacques. 2012. The phonology of Laze: phonemic analysis, syllabic inventory, and a short word list. Yuyanxue Luncong 语言学论丛 45: 196-230. HAL halshs-00582639v2.
sources.quote: Every syllable carries a tone slot T; three lexical tones on nouns, four on verbs; tone sandhi referred to Michaud 2009. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 24-page article (a full-text search for stress/accent/promin: zero hits outside references).
sources.locator: Section 1, p.3 ('Laze, like Naxi and Yongning Na, has a simple syllabic structure: (C)(G)V+T.. T a tone.. Tones are not included because in synchrony they combine freely with all syllable types'); endnote, p.23 ('In Laze, there are three lexical tones for nouns: High, Mid and Low, and four for verbs.. High, Mid and Low, and Mid-to-High.. see Michaud 2009 for an analysis of this tone system')
sources.note: The full published phonology of Laze (24 pp + 1,400-word list); states syllable template (C)(G)V+T and tone inventory; was not in the held src set. downloaded: confirms tonal coding, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Michaud, Alexis (米可). 2009. 木里水田话声调系统研究 [A study of the tone system of Muli Shuitian (Laze)]. Minzu Yuwen 民族语文 2009(6): 28-33. HAL halshs-00436463v2.
sources.quote: Published version of the 2008 analysis: level-tone system (3 tones on nouns, 4 on verbs, 6 disyllabic patterns), tone change has grammatical function; some clitics are lexically toneless and receive tone by spreading. No 重音 (stress) anywhere in the text.
sources.locator: p.2-3 (abstract: '本文着重探讨木里水田话声调系统'; section 1: monosyllabic nouns have three level tones H/M/L, verbs H/M/L plus the composite MH; fn.4 cites Huang Bufan 2009 木里水田话概况; p.3 note: Huang recorded four tones 35/53/33/31 in Bowa); p.4 (grammatical word /bi/ '在词汇层次上无声调' = lexically toneless, tone spreading over toneless syllables within the phonological word); p.5 (six tone patterns on disyllabic nouns).

sources.citation: Michaud, Alexis. 2011. The tones of numerals and numeral-plus-classifier phrases: on structural similarities between Naxi, Na and Laze. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 34(1): 1-26. HAL halshs-00582721.
sources.quote: Treats Laze numeral phrases purely in terms of H/M/L tone patterns; silent on stress.

sources.note: Independent (non-Michaud) areal-typological characterisation: within the Na languages there is a south-to-north cline from omnisyllabic tone systems (Naxi) to restricted tone systems with neutralization of tonal contrasts (Yongning Na, Laze); Yi and Na groups otherwise have omnisyllabic tonal systems. No tone inventory given for Laze (relies on Huang 2009 and Michaud).
